p: וּבְשַׁבָּת כְּתִיב וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וְגוֹמֵר וּבְתַרְגּוּם יְרוּשַׁלְמִי וַחֲמֵיד וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט) עוֹלָמִי עוֹלָמִי הַלְוַאי תְּהֵא מַעֲלַת חֵן לְפָנַי בְּכָל עֵת כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהֶעֱלֵית חֵן לְפָנַי בְּשָׁעָה זוֹ.

— Regarding Shabbat it is written, “God completed on the seventh day ….” The Jerusalem Targum renders this “He desired.” This follows the statement in Bereishit Rabbah (chapter 9): “My world, My world, may you always find favor before Me as you have found favor before Me at this moment.”

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת מָצְאָה הַבְּרִיאָה חֵן בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְשָׂמַח אָז בְּמַעֲשָׂיו כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד דִּכְתִיב יִשְׂמַח הַשֵּׁם בְּמַעֲשָׂיו וְאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ) שָׂמַח הַשֵּׁם בְּמַעֲשָׂיו אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר אֶלָּא יִשְׂמַח עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי.

— On Shabbat, creation found favor in Hashem’s eyes, and He then rejoiced in His works, as will occur in the future. It is written, “Hashem will rejoice in His works,” and the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 20): It does not say “Hashem rejoiced in His works,” but “will rejoice”; in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will, and so forth.

וּכְתִיב וַיִּשְׁבּוֹת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ שְׁבִיתָה וּמְנוּחָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינַת שִׂמְחָה שֶׁמָּצִינוּ מְנוּחָה שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הָעֶצֶב כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ הַשֵּׁם לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וְגוֹמֵר וְזֶהוּ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ הַנִּזְכָּר וְכָל חֵידוּ.

— It is written, “He rested on the seventh day from all His work.” Cessation and rest are also an aspect of joy, for we find that rest is the opposite of sorrow, as it is said, “On the day Hashem grants you rest from your sorrow ….” This is the aforementioned holy Zohar’s expression on this portion, “and all joy.”

h: Blessing Holiness and the Two Lights

p: וּכְתִיב וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.
— It is written, “God blessed the seventh day.”

וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּבִרְכַּת הַשַּׁבָּת כּוֹלֵל רָאשֵׁי הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁהֵם חַיֵּי בָנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר פָּרָשַׁת חַיֵּי שָׁם) וְזֶהוּ כָּל בִּרְכָאן שֶׁכּוֹלֵל שָׁלֹשׁ הַבְּרָכוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.

— We have already explained that Shabbat’s blessing encompasses the principal blessings: life, children, and sustenance (as explained there in Chayei Sarah). This is “all blessings,” encompassing the three blessings mentioned above.
וּכְתִיב וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה הַיְינוּ חָכְמָה דְּאִקְרֵי קוֹדֶשׁ.
— It is written, “He sanctified it.” Holiness means Chokhmah, wisdom, which is called kodesh.
חָכְמָה עִלָּאָה קוֹדֶשׁ עִלָּאָה חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה קוֹדֶשׁ תַּתָּאָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קעו ב וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
— Supernal wisdom is supernal holiness, and lower wisdom is lower holiness (Zohar III, 176b, and elsewhere).
וְחָכְמָה הוּא אוֹר וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג) חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים אוֹרָה כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי
— Wisdom is light, as the Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 3): the five occurrences of light correspond to the five books of the Torah, and so forth.
וְאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דִּכְוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פו:)
— The light of the Written Torah belongs to Shabbat, since all agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat (Shabbat 86b).
וְאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז ב) בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאִיהוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי
— Regarding the light of the Oral Torah, it is stated (Zohar I, 47b), “On the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרִינָן לָהּ.
— As it is written, “Malkhut is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah.”
וְזֶהוּ וְעַל חֲדָא תַּרְתֵּי נְהוֹרָא לָהּ יִמְטֵי.
— This is “May twofold light reach her.”

וְהַיְינוּ אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא אוֹר הַגָּנוּז לַעֲמֵלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ ג) וְהוּא מְרוּמָז בְּקוֹצָא דְּיוּד דִּלְעֵילָא דִּרְמִיזָא לְאַיִן שֶׁהוּא כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן וְכַנִּזְכָּר מֵהַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.

— This is the light of the Oral Torah, from the dew of Atika, the light hidden for those who labor in the Oral Torah (as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3). It is alluded to in the upper tip of the yud, which alludes to Ayin, nothingness, the supernal crown, as cited above from the holy Zohar.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 176b: ““They rose before Moses.” The companions have explained this verse. Rabbi Shimon said: “Those summoned to the assembly”—keri’ei is written without a yod. Why keri’ei? Rather, earthly kingship is like heavenly kingship. Its mystery is this: all those supernal crowns to which the holy Name is joined are summoned from the place called Holiness, as it is written: “Holy convocations.” When? When a festival is appointed in the world. Just as those supernal crowns are summoned from the upper Holiness, so the lower Holiness summons its hosts, to crown and elevate them. The upper Holiness is known; the lower Holiness is Solomon’s wisdom. It too summons all its hosts, and all those hosts are summoned to be crowned in this lower Holiness when a festival rests upon the world. Just as its hosts stand above, so the leaders of the people stand below in its likeness. Therefore they are called “those summoned to the assembly.” Because they are below, keri’ei is written defectively; yet they possess greater completeness.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 3:5: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction, 17a: “In this arrangement they are called: Chesed, the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferet, the torso; Netzach and Hod, the two legs; Yesod, the body’s extremity, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchut, the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah. Chokhmah is the brain, inward thought. Binah is the heart, through which the heart understands. Of these two it is written, ‘The concealed things belong to the Lord our God.’ The upper Keter is the royal crown, of which it says, ‘Declaring the end from the beginning.’ It is the skull of the tefillin; another reading says, the skull that does not put on tefillin. Within is yod-he-vav-he, the path of emanation.”

p: וּכְתִיב כִּי בוֹ שָׁבַת מִכָּל וְגוֹמֵר אַף שֶׁכְּבָר נֶאֱמַר וַיִּשְׁבּוֹת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִכָּל וְגוֹמֵר.
— It is written, “For on it He rested from all …,” although it had already said, “He rested on the seventh day from all ….”
אַךְ הַמְכוּוָּן דְּאַף שֶׁכְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ מֵהַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׂמַח אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר אֶלָּא יִשְׂמַח וְכוּלֵי וְכָאן אוֹמֵר וַיִּשְׁבּוֹת וְגוֹמֵר וּשְׁבִיתָה וּמְנוּחָה הוּא שִׂמְחָה כָּאָמוּר.

— The intention is this: although we have quoted Midrash Rabbah that it does not say “rejoiced,” but “will rejoice,” and so forth, here it says, “He rested …,” and cessation and rest are joy, as explained.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת מָצְאָה הַבְּרִיאָה חֵן בְּעֵינָיו וְשָׂמַח הַשֵּׁם בְּמַעֲשָׂיו דְּשַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּהָרוֹאֶה.

— It therefore explains that on Shabbat creation found favor in His eyes, and Hashem rejoiced in His works, because Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come, as the Sages said in the chapter HaRo’eh.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי בוֹ שָׁבַת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ וְשָׂמַח הַשֵּׁם בְּמַעֲשָׂיו.
— Thus it is said, “For on it He rested from all His work,” and Hashem rejoiced in His works.

אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים לַעֲשׂוֹת שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית צְרִיכִין תִּיקּוּן אֲפִילּוּ אָדָם צָרִיךְ תִּיקּוּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא) וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְהָאָדָם שֶׁיְתַקֵּן וְיִהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד וְעַל כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא מָצָא הַבְּרִיאָה חֵן בְּעֵינָיו וְשָׂמַח הַשֵּׁם בְּמַעֲשָׂיו.

— “Which God created to be made”: everything made in creation requires rectification; even man requires rectification, as the Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 11). Man was given the task of rectifying it so that it would be very good. Therefore, on Shabbat, a foretaste of the World to Come, creation found favor in His eyes and Hashem rejoiced in His works.

p: וְהִנֵּה כְתִיב וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אוֹתוֹ וְלֹא כְתִיב אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.
— It is written, “He sanctified it,” rather than explicitly saying “the seventh day.”
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאוֹמְרִים בֵּרַכְתּוֹ מִכָּל הַיָּמִים וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים.
— This follows our prayer, “You blessed it above all days and sanctified it above all seasons.”
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשַׁבָּת כּוֹלֵל כָּל בִּרְכוֹת שֵׁשֶׁת הַיָּמִים וּקְדוּשַּׁת כָּל הַזְּמַנִּים.
— Shabbat encompasses all the blessings of the six days and the holiness of all the sacred seasons.

וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח א) דְּהַהוּא יוֹמָא מִתְבָּרְכָאן מִינֵיהּ כָּל שִׁיתָא יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין אַף דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית הֵם שֵׁשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּדַיֵּיק בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִדִּכְתִיב כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְתִיב בְּשֵׁשֶׁת.

— It is stated (Zohar II, 88a) that from that day all six supernal days are blessed. The six days of creation are the six attributes, as the holy Zohar infers from the wording “For six days He made,” rather than “in six days.”
וְאוֹת וָא״ו שֶׁבְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה תִּפְאֶרֶת כָּלִיל שִׁית סְפִירָאן הֵ״א מַלְכוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רנח א) וָא״ו קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הֵ״א שְׁכִינְתָּא.
— The vav in the Name Havayah is Tiferet, encompassing six sefirot, while heh is Malkhut, as the holy Zohar states (III, 258a): “Vav is the Holy One, blessed be He; heh is the Shekhinah.”
וּבְחִינַת וָא״ו גָּבוֹהַ מִבְּחִינַת הֵ״א תַּתָּאָה וְקוֹדֵם.
— The aspect of vav is higher than the lower heh and precedes it.

אָכֵן לְמַעְלָה שֵׁשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת גְּבוֹהִין מִמִּדַּת מַלְכוּת אֲבָל אֵינָם מַשְׁפִּיעִין לְמַטָּה רַק עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת מַלְכוּת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הֶחָדָשׁ (בַּתִּיקּוּנִים דפ״ו קיא א) וְכָל סְפִירָה אֵין לָהּ פְּעוּלָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה וְכוּלֵי עַיֵּן שָׁם.

— Indeed, above, the six attributes are higher than Malkhut, but they bestow influence below only through Malkhut. As stated in the Zohar Chadash (Tikkunim, דפ״ו edition, 111a), no sefirah acts in the lower realms except through Malkhut, of which it is said, “His kingship rules over all,” and so forth; see there.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יָמִים יוּצָּרוּ וְלוֹ אֶחָד בָּהֶם זֶה יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה) שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ בְּחִינַת כָּל הַשֵּׁשׁ מִדּוֹת לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וְעַל יְדֵי יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת מְקַבְּלִין כָּל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מִקְּדוּשַּׁת הַמִּדּוֹת דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ.

— Thus it is said, “Days were formed, and one among them is His”: this is the day of Shabbat for Israel (as stated at the beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah). Hashem bestows all six attributes upon Shabbat, and through Shabbat all six weekdays receive the holiness of the attributes, each day its due.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בֵּיצָה טז.) שֶׁהִלֵּל מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ וְכוּלֵי שֶׁאָמַר בָּרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם יוֹם יוֹם וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (בְּרָכוֹת מ.) כָּל יוֹם וָיוֹם תֵּן לוֹ מֵעֵין בִּרְכוֹתָיו.

— The Sages said (Beitzah 16a) that Hillel had a different practice, and so forth, saying, “Blessed is Hashem day by day.” This accords with the exposition (Berakhot 40a): “Each day, give Him blessings appropriate to that day.”
שֶׁכָּל יוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּרָכָה מְיוּחֶדֶת מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַמִּדָּה שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ.
— Each day has its distinctive blessing from the holy root of its corresponding attribute.
וְשַׁמַּאי הָיָה אוֹכֵל כָּל יָמָיו לִכְבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת כָּאָמוּר שֶׁכָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַיָּמִים וּבִרְכוֹתֵיהֶן בָּא וְנִכְלָל בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת.
— Shammai ate throughout his life in honor of Shabbat, for, as explained, all the days’ holiness and blessings enter and are included in the holiness of Shabbat.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְלוֹ אֶחָד בָּהֶם דַּיְיקָא שֶׁבִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מוֹפִיעַ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִשְׁפָּע בָּהֶם בִּרְכַּת הַיָּמִים וְזֶהוּ בֵּרַכְתּוֹ מִכָּל הַיָּמִים.

— Thus, specifically, “And one among them is His”: the holiness of Shabbat shines within the weekdays. Israel accepts the attribute of His blessed kingship, and through this the days’ blessing is bestowed upon them. This is “You blessed it above all days.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 258a: “The tefillin of the Master of the world are Keter. What is the Keter of the Master of the world? Havayah: yod is Chokhmah; heh is Binah; vav is Tiferet, encompassing six sefirot; heh is Malkhut. Therefore: “Who is like Your people Israel,” and, “What great nation has a god near to it, as Hashem our God whenever we call to Him?” The four passages are all inscribed in kaf, the mystery of the letter kaf: two yods, the two yods of Yod-Alef-Heh-Dalet-Vav-Nun-Heh-Yod, “each spoon of ten shekels, by the sacred shekel.” The kaf of Keter comprises ten sefirot included from above downward and ten sefirot from below upward.”

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 1:2: ““Days were formed, and one of them is His”—this is the day of Shabbat for Israel. How so? A person works for six days and rests on the seventh, finding reconciliation with his children and household. Again, a person works in the presence of his enemies for six days and rests on the seventh, forgetting all the suffering he endured. Such is human nature: a good day causes one to forget a bad day, and a bad day causes one to forget a good day. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work for six days, Shabbat should be entirely devoted to Torah. Hence they said: A person should rise early and study on Shabbat, go to the synagogue and study hall, read Torah and study the Prophets, and then go home and eat and drink, fulfilling “Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who engage in Torah, as it says, “My hand made all these … but to this one I will look: to the poor and broken in spirit who trembles at My word.””

Its explanation is that the nations count the days of the week for the sake of the days themselves, calling each day by a name of its own, whereas Israel count all the days toward Shabbat, ‘one in Shabbat,’ ‘second in Shabbat,’ for this is part of the commandment to remember it constantly, every day. … And I say that this is the exposition of Shammai the Elder, who explained the commandment ‘Remember’ as ‘before it comes.’ The baraita mentions, in addition, his measure of piety: he remembered it even in his food and ate in honor of Shabbat all the days of his life. Hillel himself agrees with Shammai's exposition, but he had a different measure in matters of food, for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven, and he trusted in Hashem that He would provide him for Shabbat a portion finer than that of all the days.”

h: The Festivals and the Six Attributes

p: וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁכָּל שֵׁשֶׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים נֶגֶד שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
— “You sanctified it above all seasons” follows what I heard from our holy master, of righteous and holy memory: all six festivals correspond to the six weekdays.
פֶּסַח וְשָׁבוּעוֹת כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וּרְבִיעִי.
— Passover and Shavuot correspond to the first and fourth days.
רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כְּנֶגֶד שֵׁנִי חֲמִישִׁי.
— Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur correspond to the second and fifth.
סוּכּוֹת וּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת נֶגֶד יוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי שִׁשִּׁי.
— Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret correspond to the third and sixth days.
וְהַמְכוּוָּן הוּא דְּפֶסַח הוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלּוֹ נֶאֱמַר גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְהַגְּאוּלָה.
— The meaning is that Passover corresponds to our patriarch Abraham, peace be upon him, to whom the Egyptian exile and redemption were foretold.
וְהָיָה רַק עַל יְדֵי הַחֶסֶד שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אַבְרָהָם חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם.
— This came about only through lovingkindness, Abraham’s aspect: “lovingkindness to Abraham.”
וְהוּא נֶגֶד יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד.
— It corresponds to the first day, whose attribute is Chesed.
וּבוֹ נֶאֱמַר מַאֲמָר יְהִי אוֹר וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב) יְהִי אוֹר זֶה אַבְרָהָם.
— On it the utterance “Let there be light” was spoken, and the Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 2), “Let there be light”—this is Abraham.
שָׁבוּעוֹת נֶגֶד יוֹם רְבִיעִי שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת נֶצַח וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדָּה זוֹ וְחַג זֶה נֶגְדּוֹ שֶׁהוֹרִיד הַתּוֹרָה לָאָרֶץ.
— Shavuot corresponds to the fourth day, the attribute of Netzach. Moses our teacher is the vehicle for this attribute, and this festival corresponds to him, for he brought the Torah down to earth.
רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נֶגֶד יוֹם שֵׁנִי גְּבוּרָה דְּאִיתָא (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מא) תַּמָּן תִּשְׁרֵי וְדָא דְּרוֹעָא תִּנְיָינָא יוֹם תִּנְיָינָא וְכוּלֵי אִיהוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
— Rosh Hashanah corresponds to the second day, Gevurah, for it is stated (Tikkunei Zohar, tikkun 41), “There is Tishrei, and this is the second arm, the second day … it is Rosh Hashanah.”
יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נֶגֶד יוֹם חֲמִישִׁי שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הוֹד דַּרְגָּא דְּאַהֲרֹן כַּיָּדוּעַ וְאַהֲרֹן הוּא הַמְכַפֵּר בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
— Yom Kippur corresponds to the fifth day, the attribute of Hod, Aaron’s level, as is known. Aaron is the one who effects atonement on Yom Kippur.

וְסוּכּוֹת נֶגֶד יוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת תִּפְאֶרֶת וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדָּה זוֹ אוֹת וָא״ו דְּאִקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רֵישׁ וַיִּקְרָא) וּכְתִיב תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב.

— Sukkot corresponds to the third day, the attribute of Tiferet. Our patriarch Jacob, peace be upon him, is the vehicle for this attribute, the letter vav, called the letter of truth, as stated in the holy Zohar (beginning of Vayikra). It is written, “You will give truth to Jacob.”
וְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת נֶגְדּוֹ דִּכְתִיב וְיַעֲקֹב נָסַע סוּכֹּתָה.
— The festival of Sukkot corresponds to him, for it is written, “Jacob traveled to Sukkot.”
וְיוֹם שִׁשִּׁי שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם שֶׁיּוֹסֵף מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדָּה זוֹ וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת
— The sixth day is the attribute of “the righteous one, foundation of the world,” whose vehicle is Joseph; Shemini Atzeret corresponds to him.
דְּסוּכּוֹת וּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת סְמוּכִין זֶה לָזֶה דְּיַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף כַּחֲדָא אִינּוּן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קעו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
— Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret are adjacent because “Jacob and Joseph are as one” (Zohar I, 176b, end).
וְתַרְוַויְיהוּ כַּחֲדָא אָזְלֵי וְדָא הוּא רָזָא דְּאַת וָא״ו דְּאָזְלֵי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ כַּחֲדָא (שָׁם קפב ב)
— “They both go together, and this is the mystery of the letter vav, for both go together” (there, 182b).
דְּיַעֲקֹב אוֹת וָא״ו אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב וּבְחִינַת יוֹסֵף וָא״ו זְעֵירָא וָא״ו הַמִּילּוּי.
— Jacob is the letter vav, “truth to Jacob,” while Joseph’s aspect is the small vav, the second vav in the letter’s spelled-out form.

וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאוֹמְרִים וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁבִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת נִכְלָלִים כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת שֵׁשֶׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים וְהַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁהֵם קְדוּשַּׁת שֵׁשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת כָּאָמוּר וְעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת מְקַבְּלִים קְדוּשָּׁתָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.

— Thus we say, “You sanctified it above all seasons”: Shabbat’s holiness includes the holiness of all six festivals and sacred seasons, the holiness of the six attributes, as explained. Through the holiness of Shabbat they receive their holiness, as we have said.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אוֹתוֹ אוֹת וָא״ו שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נִיתַּן הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְשֵׁשֶׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
— This is “He sanctified oto,” read as “the letter vav”: through it holiness is given to the six festivals, corresponding to the six weekdays.
